sn12.23:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I say that the destruction of the taints is for one who knows and sees, not for one who does not know and does not see.
sn12.23:1.3: For one who knows what, for one who sees what, does the destruction of the taints come about?
sn12.23:1.4: ‘Such is form, such its origin, such its passing away;
sn12.23:1.8: such is consciousness, such its origin, such its passing away’:
sn12.23:1.9: it is for one who knows thus, for one who sees thus, that the destruction of the taints comes about.
sn12.23:2.1: “I say, bhikkhus, that the knowledge of destruction in regard to destruction has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:2.2: And what is the proximate cause for the knowledge of destruction?
sn12.23:2.4: “I say, bhikkhus, that liberation too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:2.5: And what is the proximate cause for liberation?
sn12.23:2.7: “I say, bhikkhus, that dispassion too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:2.8: And what is the proximate cause for dispassion?
sn12.23:2.10: “I say, bhikkhus, that revulsion too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:2.11: And what is the proximate cause for revulsion?
sn12.23:2.12: It should be said: the knowledge and vision of things as they really are.
sn12.23:2.13: “I say, bhikkhus, that the knowledge and vision of things as they really are too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:2.14: And what is the proximate cause for the knowledge and vision of things as they really are?
sn12.23:2.16: “I say, bhikkhus, that concentration too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:3.1: And what is the proximate cause for concentration?
sn12.23:3.3: “I say, bhikkhus, that happiness too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:3.4: And what is the proximate cause for happiness?
sn12.23:3.6: “I say, bhikkhus, that tranquillity too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:3.7: And what is the proximate cause for tranquillity?
sn12.23:3.9: “I say, bhikkhus, that rapture too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:3.10: And what is the proximate cause for rapture?
sn12.23:3.12: “I say, bhikkhus, that gladness too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:3.13: And what is the proximate cause for gladness?
sn12.23:3.15: “I say, bhikkhus, that faith too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:4.1: And what is the proximate cause for faith?
sn12.23:4.3: “I say, bhikkhus, that suffering too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:4.4: And what is the proximate cause for suffering?
sn12.23:4.6: “I say, bhikkhus, that birth too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:4.7: And what is the proximate cause for birth?
sn12.23:4.9: “I say, bhikkhus, that existence too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:4.10: And what is the proximate cause for existence?
sn12.23:4.12: “I say, bhikkhus, that clinging too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:4.13: And what is the proximate cause for clinging?
sn12.23:4.15: “I say, bhikkhus, that craving too has a proximate cause; it does not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:5.1: And what is the proximate cause for craving?
sn12.23:5.3: “For feeling, it should be said: contact. For contact:
sn12.23:5.4: the six sense bases. For the six sense bases:
sn12.23:5.8: “I say, bhikkhus, that volitional formations too have a proximate cause; they do not lack a proximate cause.
sn12.23:5.9: And what is the proximate cause for volitional formations?
sn12.23:6.1: “Thus, bhikkhus, with ignorance as proximate cause, volitional formations come to be;
sn12.23:6.2: with volitional formations as proximate cause, consciousness;
sn12.23:6.3: with consciousness as proximate cause, name-and-form;
sn12.23:6.4: with name-and-form as proximate cause, the six sense bases;
sn12.23:6.5: with the six sense bases as proximate cause, contact;
sn12.23:6.6: with contact as proximate cause, feeling;
sn12.23:6.7: with feeling as proximate cause, craving;
sn12.23:6.8: with craving as proximate cause, clinging;
sn12.23:6.9: with clinging as proximate cause, existence;
sn12.23:6.10: with existence as proximate cause, birth;
sn12.23:6.11: with birth as proximate cause, suffering;
sn12.23:6.12: with suffering as proximate cause, faith;
sn12.23:6.13: with faith as proximate cause, gladness;
sn12.23:6.14: with gladness as proximate cause, rapture;
sn12.23:6.15: with rapture as proximate cause, tranquillity;
sn12.23:6.16: with tranquillity as proximate cause, happiness;
sn12.23:6.17: with happiness as proximate cause, concentration;
sn12.23:6.18: with concentration as proximate cause, the knowledge and vision of things as they really are;
sn12.23:6.19: with the knowledge and vision of things as they really are as proximate cause, revulsion;
sn12.23:6.20: with revulsion as proximate cause, dispassion;
sn12.23:6.21: with dispassion as proximate cause, liberation;
sn12.23:6.22: with liberation as proximate cause, the knowledge of destruction.
sn12.23:7.1: “Just as, bhikkhus, when rain pours down in thick droplets on a mountain top, the water flows down along the slope and fills the cleft, gullies, and creeks; these being full fill up the pools; these being full fill up the lakes; these being full fill up the streams; these being full fill up the rivers; and these being full fill up the great ocean;
sn12.23:8.1: so too, with ignorance as proximate cause, volitional formations come to be; with volitional formations as proximate cause, consciousness … with liberation as proximate cause, the knowledge of destruction.”
